hook: A cold pack in a first-aid kit gets icy the moment you squeeze it, yet nothing pushes the salt inside to dissolve. Ice melts on a warm day even though melting absorbs heat. Neither enthalpy nor entropy alone predicts these. Gibbs free energy combines the two into one number that does.

prereq.q: What is the sign of ΔH for an exothermic reaction?
prereq.why: Exothermic means the system releases heat to the surroundings, so ΔH < 0.

prereq.q: What is the unit of a standard entropy change, ΔS°?
prereq.why: Entropies are tabulated in joules per mole per kelvin.

figure.caption: The signs of ΔH° and ΔS° decide whether a process is favored at all temperatures, at low T, at high T or at none.

chain.cause: Releasing heat (ΔH < 0) spreads energy into the surroundings and raises their entropy
chain.effect: a negative ΔH° makes a process more likely to be favored

chain.cause: Dispersing the system’s own matter or energy (ΔS > 0) raises the system’s entropy
chain.effect: a positive ΔS° also makes a process more likely to be favored

chain.cause: Gibbs free energy weighs both, ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS°
chain.effect: a process is thermodynamically favored when ΔG° < 0

chain.cause: The entropy term is multiplied by T
chain.effect: temperature decides which term wins when the two disagree, and T = ΔH°/ΔS° is where they balance

ideas: ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS°. A process is thermodynamically favored when ΔG° < 0.
Make units match: ΔS° from J/(mol·K) to kJ/(mol·K) (÷ 1000), and T in kelvin.
ΔH° < 0, ΔS° > 0: favored at all T. ΔH° > 0, ΔS° < 0: not favored at any T. Same signs: temperature decides.
When the signs agree, the crossover is T = ΔH°/ΔS°, where ΔG° = 0.
ΔG°<sub>rxn</sub> = Σ nΔG°f(products) − Σ nΔG°f(reactants); ΔG°f of an element in its standard state is 0.

misconception.wrong: An endothermic process is never favored, or an exothermic one always is.
misconception.right: Favorability depends on ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS°. An endothermic process is favored when TΔS° > ΔH° (ice melting above 0 °C); an exothermic one with ΔS° < 0 stops being favored at high temperature.

summary: Gibbs free energy, ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS°, decides thermodynamic favorability: a process is favored when ΔG° < 0. Match the units (kJ and J) and use kelvin. The signs of ΔH° and ΔS° tell you whether a process is favored at all temperatures, none, or only above or below T = ΔH°/ΔS°.
